oneLiner: The only commercial supplier of quantum annealers, now also funding a gate-model program, with revenue still in the low millions per quarter. The market is betting that one record system order and a federal equity stake mark the start of repeatable system sales rather than a one-off.

verdict.summary: Q3 2026 answered the wrong half of the question: recurring revenue grew, but bookings of $1.9M did not refill a backlog that still rests mostly on one $20M university system. The equity is an option on system sales repeating, held against an adjusted EBITDA loss near $38M a quarter and a reverse DCF that needs revenue to grow about 118% a year for 8 years versus 51% a year delivered. Our base case sits below the current price, the bear case far below and the bull case about double, so the probability-weighted value is slightly under today: the cash pile limits the downside but does not pay for it. We would turn constructive if the Florida Atlantic system is recognized in Q4 2026 and at least one new multi-million system order is booked by the Q1 2027 report; we would turn negative if the delivery slips into 2027 or bookings stay below revenue for two more quarters.
wtb: The $20M Florida Atlantic University system is delivered in Q4 2026 and Q4 revenue is at least ~$15M (Siberforge estimate), reported around March 2027.
At least two new system orders are booked by mid-2027, so FY2027 revenue exceeds ~$50M against $38.3M of total RPO at Sep 30, 2026.
Adjusted EBITDA loss holds near $40M a quarter, leaving more than ~$300M of cash at end-2027 without equity issuance beyond the Commerce stake.
Revenue then compounds at roughly 118% a year for 8 years (the reverse-DCF bar), more than double the 51% a year delivered over the last three fiscal years.

bear.why: FY2027 revenue ~$30M: the Florida Atlantic installation tail and QCaaS, but no new system orders, as the pipeline fails to convert and classical solvers keep matching annealing. Burn continues near $170M a year. The market stops paying for optionality and values the business at ~30x sales (EV ~$0.9B) plus ~$250M of remaining cash.

base.why: FY2027 revenue ~$50M: one or two new Advantage2 system sales on top of RPO conversion and QCaaS growing 40-50%. CHIPS milestones start to pay and burn stays flat. The multiple compresses to ~65x sales (EV ~$3.25B) as revenue roughly doubles - still a scarcity premium, but below today's because losses are unchanged.

bull.why: FY2027 revenue ~$90M, above the ~$81M consensus: the tripled pipeline converts into system sales every quarter, a second Fortune 100 production contract lands and the 17-qubit gate-model system ships with paid orders. A sector re-rating pays ~90x sales (EV ~$8.1B) for visible triple-digit growth.

scenarioModel.note: Value per share = (FY2027 revenue x EV/Sales + net cash) / shares. Revenue is $30M / $50M / $90M (the table rounds to $0.0-0.1B). The page adds net cash implied by its market data (~$875M, which predates the $252.8M Quantum Circuits payment) on ~380M shares. Actual cash was $503.4M at Sep 30, 2026 and we expect ~$250M / ~$300M / ~$350M of net cash at end-2027 after burn and partial CHIPS receipts (Siberforge estimate, unverified), so the multiples shown are the true end-2027 EV/Sales (~30x / ~65x / ~90x) reduced to offset that overstatement. Check: bear ($0.9B + $0.25B) / 380M = ~$3; base ($3.25B + $0.30B) / 380M = ~$9.4; bull ($8.1B + $0.35B) / 380M = ~$22. Dilution beyond today's count (including the Commerce shares) is not modelled, which flatters every case. Inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Is the 2026 bookings jump the start of repeatable system sales, or one university order?
debates.bull: Management said on the Nov 10 call that the dollar value of the sales pipeline rose more than 75% since the end of Q2 and more than tripled since end-2025, driven by system interest; a second Advantage2 was shipped to Como, Italy in Q3 and commercial enterprises were 52% of Q3 revenue versus 31% a year earlier.
debates.bear: Q3 bookings were $1.9M, down 19% YoY and less than half of the quarter's revenue, and RPO slipped to $38.3M from $40.7M at June 30. Nine-month bookings of $37.4M are roughly 80% two Q1 deals. A securities class action filed Oct 15 alleges the record bookings came mostly from two older contracts (per TIKR; allegations unproven).
debates.view: One order does not make a trend, and Q3 was the first chance to show a second - it did not. We will not pay for the base case until bookings exceed revenue again. Pipeline dollars are not bookings.

signpost.threshold: constructive if Q4 2026 plus Q1 2027 bookings exceed ~$20M with a named system order; bearish if RPO falls below ~$30M by Mar 31, 2027

debates.q: Does the cash last until revenue matters, or does dilution fill the gap?
debates.bull: Cash and marketable securities of $503.4M at Sep 30 cover more than three years of the current ~$145M annualized operating cash use, and up to $100M of milestone-based CHIPS funding arrives on top; adjusted EBITDA loss was flat QoQ at $37.7M, so spending has stopped accelerating.
debates.bear: Operating losses run about 15x revenue (TTM operating loss ~$196M on ~$13.2M of revenue), nine-month operating cash use of $109.0M is already above all of FY2025, capex has risen to roughly two-thirds of revenue, and the quality check flags +22.7% YoY diluted shares. The CHIPS money is itself paid for in stock.
debates.view: Solvency is not the issue through 2028; ownership is. With burn near $170M a year including capex, the company will likely raise again before revenue covers costs, and it has historically done so into strength. We treat ~5-10% annual dilution as the baseline that the scenario values do not include.

signpost.metric: Adjusted EBITDA loss and weighted share count
signpost.threshold: constructive if the quarterly loss stays at or below ~$40M with share growth under 5% YoY; bearish on a new ATM or a loss above ~$45M

debates.q: Can annealing grow fast enough to meet what the price implies?
debates.bull: QCaaS revenue grew 56% YoY to $2.2M in Q3 and production use is spreading: NTT DOCOMO deployed a second application that cut peak location-registration signals by 65.3%, and a Fortune 100 engagement drove professional services up 318% to $2.0M. The gate-model program adds a second route, with a 17-qubit system on track and delivery orders under discussion for 2027.
debates.bear: The reverse DCF needs ~118% annual revenue growth for 8 years; nine-month 2026 revenue is down 52% YoY and the recurring lines together run at ~$17M annualized. Independent benchmarks still show classical heuristics matching annealers on many commercial problems, and the gate-model roadmap targets a first error-corrected logical qubit only in 2028 and 100 logical qubits in 2032.
debates.view: The recurring core is real but small; system sales have to do the compounding, which sends this debate back to debate 1. We read QCaaS growth above 50% as necessary, not sufficient, and give the gate-model program no value before paid orders exist.

signpost.metric: QCaaS revenue growth YoY; first paid gate-model system order
signpost.threshold: QCaaS above +50% YoY through mid-2027 = on track; below +30% = recurring thesis stalling

thesis: The backlog is contracted. RPO of $38.3M at Sep 30, 2026 is about three times trailing revenue, with ~59% scheduled to be recognized within 12 months and ~71% within 24 months - the first time D-Wave has entered a year with visible revenue (debate 1).

The recurring core is compounding. QCaaS and professional services together were $4.2M of Q3 revenue, more than double a year earlier, and more than 100 customers generated revenue in the quarter (debate 3).

Washington is now a shareholder. The definitive CHIPS and Science Act agreement gives access to up to $100M in milestone-based installments for a 100,000-qubit annealer and a 10,000-qubit gate-model system, and makes the Department of Commerce a minority, non-controlling holder - a signal to other government buyers.
The balance sheet buys time. With more than $500M of cash and securities and little debt, D-Wave can fund both platforms through 2028 without being forced to sell stock at a low (debate 2).

latestQuarter.label: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30, 2026; reported Nov 10, 2026)
points: Revenue $4.51M, +21% YoY; nine-month revenue $10.45M, -52% YoY against a 2025 period that included a system sale.
QCaaS $2.2M (+56%); professional services $2.0M (+318%); systems and other ~$0.36M.
GAAP gross margin 52.9% (from 71.4%); non-GAAP 63.6% (from 77.7%), on a higher services mix.
GAAP operating expenses $55.9M (+84%); operating loss $53.5M; adjusted EBITDA loss $37.7M; net loss $48.2M ($0.13 per share).
Bookings $1.9M (-19% YoY); nine-month bookings $37.4M (+611%); RPO $38.3M versus $2.9M a year earlier.
Cash and marketable securities $503.4M; nine-month operating cash use $109.0M; 374.1M weighted shares (+9.3% YoY).

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Nov 10). Revenue of $4.51M rose 21% YoY on recurring lines - QCaaS $2.2M and professional services $2.0M - while systems revenue was only ~$0.36M, so nine-month revenue of $10.45M is still down 52%. The cost base is unchanged from Q2: GAAP operating expenses of $55.9M (+84% YoY, with Quantum Circuits absorbed) produced a $53.5M operating loss and a $37.7M adjusted EBITDA loss; the $48.2M net loss only looks better than last year's $140.0M because a $121.9M warrant charge is gone. Bookings were $1.9M and RPO eased to $38.3M. Cash fell $42.9M in the quarter to $503.4M. The definitive CHIPS agreement was signed (announced early September), but no funds had been received at quarter-end and the balance sheet carries the $100M as uncollected equity proceeds. Greg Golkov presented as acting CFO in place of John Markovich (per secondary coverage; no explanation given).
guidanceProse: D-Wave gives no dollar guidance. On the Nov 10 call management said the $20M Florida Atlantic University system is expected to be delivered in Q4 2026 with a substantial portion of revenue recognized on delivery, more over the installation period in early 2027, then smaller maintenance and cloud amounts over several years. That implies Q4 alone exceeds the first nine months and FY2026 revenue lands around $25-30M (Siberforge estimate). Consensus of ~$42.5M for FY2026 and ~$81M for FY2027 (TIKR, Nov 3) looks stale against a 12-month RPO schedule of ~$22.6M. No operating-expense outlook was given.

guide.label: FY26 revenue shape
guide.sub: no dollar guide | $20M FAU system delivers in Q4, remainder on installation in early 2027

segments: QCaaS subscriptions: the recurring core, sold direct and through the Leap cloud and hyperscaler marketplaces.
Professional services: application engagements that seed QCaaS conversions, now including paid gate-model research projects.

Systems: lumpy on-premise Advantage2 sales (Julich in H1 2025; the $20M Florida Atlantic University order booked Q1 2026; a unit shipped to Como, Italy in Q3 2026 funded by Swiss Quantum Technology SA).
competitive: IonQ posted $80.1M of Q2 2026 revenue - about 26x D-Wave's that quarter - with about $2.0B of pro forma cash; on commercial traction the gap is widening, not closing.

Rigetti ($5.1M Q2 2026 revenue) and newly listed IQM, Quantinuum and Infleqtion all sell gate-model systems; D-Wave's Quantum Circuits unit enters that race at 17 qubits versus IBM machines in the hundreds.
IBM is the gate-model benchmark, targeting its fault-tolerant Starling system for 2029; Google opened early access to the 105-qubit Willow chip in March 2026.
In annealing D-Wave is effectively unopposed among quantum vendors - the real competitor is classical: GPU-accelerated heuristics and hybrid solvers keep raising the bar an annealer must beat.
moat: D-Wave is the only commercial supplier of quantum annealers, with the 4,400-plus-qubit Advantage2 generally available since May 2025 and a genuinely recurring, if tiny, QCaaS base. What is not proven: peer-reviewed quantum advantage on commercial optimization problems versus modern classical solvers, and the gate-model program bought with Quantum Circuits in January 2026 is years behind IBM, Google and IonQ. The moat today is uniqueness of approach plus a subsidized balance sheet, not demonstrated economic value.
risks: The bar is far above the record. The quality check's reverse DCF needs revenue growth of ~118% a year for 8 years against 51% a year delivered, and year-over-year growth over the last four reported quarters ran +100%, +19%, -81%, -1% - the track record is one of lumpy system sales, not compounding (debate 3).

Losses scale faster than gross profit. Nine-month non-GAAP gross profit was $6.9M against $114.4M of adjusted operating expenses; the operating margin, operating cash flow and capex-intensity rows are all amber and nothing in the Q3 report points to operating leverage before system sales repeat (debate 2).

Dilution is chronic. Diluted shares are up 22.7% YoY on the quality check (9.3% on Q3 weighted shares) after repeated ATM programs, and the Commerce stake adds $100M of new stock whose share count and price are not disclosed (debate 2).

One customer and one delivery carry the year. Most of FY2026 revenue depends on a single university system arriving in Q4, and one customer was about 41% of revenue last quarter (per Finsee; unverified); a slip of weeks moves the year into 2027 and would lend weight to the Oct 15 class action claims (debate 1).
The technology case is still open. Classical solvers continue to match annealers on many commercial problems, and the $252.8M gate-model purchase raised costs years before it can earn revenue.
catalysts: By Dec 31, 2026: Florida Atlantic University Advantage2 delivery - the bulk of FY2026 revenue (debate 1).
Late 2026: completion of the 17-qubit gate-model system; first delivery orders discussed for 2027 (debate 3).
~Mar 2027 (date not announced): Q4 2026 report - system revenue recognized, Q4 bookings, RPO, any FY2027 framing (debates 1, 2).
H1 2027: first CHIPS milestone installments and disclosure of the Commerce share issuance terms (debate 2).
~May 2027: Q1 2027 report - whether a new system order has been booked (debate 1).
Ongoing: the securities class action filed Oct 15, 2026 over bookings disclosures (debate 1).

valPresets.note: Revenue mode is the only defensible frame: D-Wave is deeply unprofitable, so FCF-based DCF is meaningless. Presets compound a roughly $25-30M FY2026 revenue base (Siberforge estimate); even the bear case needs a 35% CAGR, and the bull case (75% a year for 8 years) is still well short of the growth the reverse DCF says is priced in. Interim burn and dilution are ignored - generous to every case.

changelog.change: Rebuilt as a v3 decision note for Q3 2026 (revenue $4.51M, bookings $1.9M, RPO $38.3M, cash $503.4M), the definitive CHIPS agreement, the Oct 15 class action and the acting-CFO change. Added FY2027 EV/Sales scenarios (bear ~$3 / base ~$9 / bull ~$22). The view did not move: still Cautious. The share price has roughly halved since August, but Q3 bookings failed to show a second system order, so the lower price is matched by weaker evidence of repeatability.

Q2 2026 note (v2): revenue $3.1M flat YoY, H1 bookings $35.5M on two deals, $100M CHIPS LOI, cash $546.2M. Lean was cautious - valuation named as the biggest risk and FY2026 framed as a single-shipment story.
